limitations_and_boundaries: GEARS must be trained on the same cell type or experimental condition for reliable predictions.
Training GEARS using combinatorial perturbation data is essential for accurate multigene prediction.
Various confounding factors such as cell cycle effects, assumed success of gene editing, and postperturbation distribution heterogeneity can influence accuracy.
GEARS may have limited ability to predict outcomes for perturbing previously unperturbed genes that are not well connected in the knowledge graph.

research_questions.statement: Can a computational method integrate deep learning with biological knowledge graphs to predict transcriptional outcomes of single and multigene perturbations, including those involving unseen genes?

provenance.text_excerpt: GEARS significantly outperformed all baselines on both datasets with an m.s.e. improvement of 30–50%

claims.statement: GEARS significantly outperforms all baseline methods in predicting single-gene perturbation transcriptional responses on both RPE-1 and K562 datasets, with m.s.e. improvement of 30-50% and Pearson correlation more than double that of baselines.

provenance.text_excerpt: GEARS improves performance by more than 30% across all cases (Fig. 2f), with the highest improvement of 53% observed when both perturbed genes in the combination are unseen.

claims.statement: GEARS outperforms baseline methods in predicting two-gene perturbation outcomes across all generalization classes, with over 30% improvement in m.s.e. and 50% greater enrichment for top DE genes.

provenance.text_excerpt: GEARS improved precision@10 by more than 40% for four of five genetic interaction subtypes

claims.statement: GEARS significantly outperforms CPA in predicting non-additive combinatorial perturbation effects across multiple genetic interaction subtypes, with correlation coefficients ~0.4 vs ~0.0, and precision@10 improvements >40% for four of five subtypes.

experiments_or_tasks: Prediction of five genetic interaction subtypes (synergy, suppression, neomorphism, redundancy, epistasis) using GEARS and comparison with CPA baseline on Norman et al. dataset.
Single-gene perturbation outcome prediction using GEARS and comparison with baseline methods (CPA, No perturbation, GRN-based) on two Perturb-seq datasets (RPE-1 and K562 cells).
Two-gene perturbation outcome prediction using GEARS on Norman et al. dataset with three generalization levels (0,1,2 unseen genes).
